theorems.title: Diagonal states are positive
theorems.statement: A normalized finite diagonal law has a nonnegative quadratic form on each complex vector.
theorems.scientific_interpretation: The positivity calculation supports the diagonal state model. Normalization is part of the law.

theorems.title: Stationarity gives a conditional step
theorems.statement: A history is fixed by the joint shift exactly when the next conditional state is the system map applied to the current state.
theorems.scientific_interpretation: An internal sequence can be consistent with global stationarity given a chosen clock.

theorems.title: Relational steps compose
theorems.statement: After n abstract clock steps, the conditional state is the system map iterated n times.
theorems.scientific_interpretation: The iteration count is an index and has no calibration on its own.

theorems.title: Shared tokens recover edges
theorems.statement: Two distinct labels share an endpoint token exactly when the abstract graph relates those labels.
theorems.scientific_interpretation: This is the combinatorial part of the analytic mutual-information realization.

theorems.title: Shortest paths satisfy the metric laws
theorems.statement: Under the path-cost laws the minimum walk cost is nonnegative, definite, symmetric and subadditive.
theorems.scientific_interpretation: The domain is one connected component. The metric is independent of an external embedding.

theorems.title: Diagonal local channels preserve remote marginals
theorems.statement: Summing over a column-normalized local channel keeps the law of the remote register fixed.
theorems.scientific_interpretation: This is the classical or diagonal specialization of the finite quantum no-signalling identity.

theorems.title: Path and triangle are nonisomorphic
theorems.statement: There is no adjacency-preserving bijection between the three-label path and triangle.
theorems.scientific_interpretation: Connectivity and subsystem count do not select a graph.

theorems.title: One preparation supports incompatible relations
theorems.statement: The same endpoint-token rule gives two nonisomorphic connected example relations on three labels.
theorems.scientific_interpretation: This is a scoped underdetermination theorem. The analytic result connects it to quantum mutual information.

theorems.title: Scaling preserves the null set
theorems.statement: For any field-valued map, nonzero scalar multiples have the same zeros.
theorems.scientific_interpretation: Null data alone leave scale undetermined on a fixed labeled vector space.

theorems.title: Scaling changes nonzero values
theorems.statement: Multiplying a nonzero field value by a scale other than one changes that value.
theorems.scientific_interpretation: Identical zeros are compatible with different interval values on the same vectors.

theorems.title: A selected boost preserves the selected interval
theorems.statement: If γ²(1−β²)=1, the specified boost preserves t²−x²−y²−z².
theorems.scientific_interpretation: Checks the algebra of supplied relativistic kinematics, which enters as a comparison assumption.
